"""A word-and-grammar approximation of completion and transition responses.

The strongest grammatical cue is an English perfect construction: a past
participle after have/has/had. Passive auxiliaries do not trigger that bonus.
Adverbs and inverted subjects may intervene, with a weaker response. Other
cues are arrival, beginnings/endings, repetition and celebrations, including
selected translations. Thinking/tool delimiters and LaTeX 'frac' are handled
separately. Unrecognized tokens predict zero; history resets per document.
"""
READS = ()

IRREGULAR_PARTICIPLES = set("""
been had become begun come done gone grown known shown taken given made found
seen heard told said read written broken chosen fallen risen gotten got
brought bought caught taught thought felt left lost kept met put set won
run held built sent spent paid sold led stood understood eaten drunk undergone
slept spoken arisen beaten bitten ridden driven hidden forgotten forgiven
frozen flown thrown drawn withdrawn worn torn born borne sworn fed wed spread
shut proven
""".split())
MODIFIERS = set("""
not never already just also always ever yet long recently previously finally
really now since often still only fully successfully actually lately even
i you he she it we they there 't ’t
""".split())
AUXILIARIES = {
    "has": 1.0, "have": 0.84, "had": 0.73, "having": 0.95,
    "hasn": 1.0, "haven": 0.84, "hadn": 0.73,
    "'ve": 0.80, "’ve": 0.86, "'s": 0.45, "’s": 0.48,
    "'d": 0.65, "’d": 0.65,
}
BOUNDED_ACTIONS = set("""
done gone come taken fallen begun started completed reached passed changed
""".split())

# One strength per familiar lexical concept, not per token identity.
WORD_CLASSES = (
    # Arriving and departing.
    (0.79, set("""
arrive arrives arriving arrived arrival coming farewell goodbye
""".split())),
    # Beginning or concluding.
    (0.51, set("""
begin begins began beginning conclude concludes concluding
开始 開始 начал comenz commenc
""".split())),
    # Imminent events.
    (0.94, set("upcoming impending forthcoming imminent underway".split())),
    # Another occurrence.
    (0.74, set("another 又 また 再次 снова 另一 另一个".split())),
    # Already / completed aspect.
    (0.62, set("已经 已經 已 уже już もう sido été".split())),
    # Arriving at a point.
    (0.60, set("到 到了 来到 来了 来到了 进入 进入了 至".split())),
    # Future morphemes.
    (0.43, set("将 將 要 未".split())),
    # Endpoints and completion.
    (0.73, set("""
结束 終わり 最后 年末 年底 月底 末 终于 開始了 开始了 过去了
""".split())),
    # Holidays and celebrations.
    (0.60, set("""
christmas thanksgiving halloween anniversary vacation holiday birthday eve
celebrate celebration celebrating festival festive festivities payday easter
ramadan hanukkah feast fête праздник празд 生日 春节 元旦 假期 放假 庆祝
""".split())),
    # Successful completion.
    (0.90, set("顺利 圆满 完工 复工复产 恢复正常".split())),
)
MARKERS = {
    "</think>": 1.06, "<tool_response>": 1.23, "<think>": 0.22,
    "<tool_call>": 0.10, "</tool_call>": -0.08, "<|im_start|>": -0.06,
    "frac": 0.60,
}


def lexical(word, last):
    if word in MARKERS:
        return MARKERS[word]
    if any(cue in word for cue in
           ("迎来", "到来", "来临", "即将", "临近", "快要")):
        return 1.50
    if word.startswith("又"):
        return 1.10 if word.endswith("要") else 0.78
    if word in {"将近", "就要"}:
        return 1.05
    if word == "eve" and last == "christmas":
        return 1.25
    for value, words in WORD_CLASSES:
        if word in words or (word.endswith("s") and word[:-1] in words):
            return value
    if word == "of" and last in {
        "end", "start", "beginning", "arrival", "anniversary", "onset"
    }:
        return 0.62
    if word == "following":
        return 0.06 if last == "the" else 0.48
    if word in {"through", "-through"}:
        return 0.60
    if word in {"approaching", "nearing", "finally", "begun"}:
        return 0.45
    if word in {"come", "comes", "came", "due"}:
        return 0.29
    if word == "been":
        return 0.19
    if word == "already":
        return 0.19
    if word in {"gone", "done", "grown", "fallen", "end"}:
        return 0.12
    return 0.0


def perfect_bonus(word, previous):
    regular = (word.isascii() and word.isalpha() and len(word) >= 4
               and word.endswith("ed")
               and word not in {"need", "feed", "seed", "reed", "weed",
                                "indeed", "hundred"})
    if word not in IRREGULAR_PARTICIPLES and not regular:
        return 0.0
    strength = 1.0
    for prior in reversed(previous):
        if prior in AUXILIARIES:
            strength *= AUXILIARIES[prior]
            break
        if prior not in MODIFIERS:
            return 0.0
        strength *= 0.40 if prior in {"always", "ever"} else 0.65
    else:
        return 0.0
    if word in {"got", "left"}:  # Often possessive "have got/left".
        strength *= 0.36
    elif word in BOUNDED_ACTIONS:
        strength *= 1.30
    return strength


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = () if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    last = previous[-1] if previous else ""
    value = lexical(word, last) + perfect_bonus(word, previous)
    if raw == "ed" and previous:
        # A split participle, e.g. "has rebound" + "ed".
        value += perfect_bonus("worked", previous[:-1])
    if word == "successfully" and last in AUXILIARIES:
        value = 0.78
    return (doc, (previous + (word,))[-4:]), float(value)

"""Approximate a small English perfect-aspect signal: past participles after have."""
READS = ()

AUXILIARIES = {
    "have", "has", "had", "having", "been", "being",
    "would", "could", "should", "might", "must",
}
IRREGULAR_PARTICIPLES = {
    "been", "become", "begun", "bent", "had", "born", "broken", "brought",
    "built", "bought", "caught", "chosen", "come", "done", "drawn",
    "driven", "eaten", "fallen", "felt", "found", "frozen", "given",
    "gone", "grown", "held", "heard", "kept", "known", "left", "lost",
    "made", "met", "paid", "put", "read", "run", "said", "seen",
    "sent", "shown", "sung", "sold", "spent", "stood", "taken", "told",
    "thought", "understood", "won", "written",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids[t]
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t - 1] != doc:
        return None, 0.0

    word = prefix.token_strings[t].strip().lower()
    # Look only a few tokens back, enough for words split by the tokenizer.
    start = t
    while start and prefix.document_ids[start - 1] == doc and t - start < 3:
        start -= 1
    previous = "".join(prefix.token_strings[start:t]).lower().rstrip()
    auxiliary = any(previous.endswith(a) for a in AUXILIARIES)
    auxiliary = auxiliary or previous.endswith(("'ve", "’ve", "'d", "’d"))
    auxiliary = auxiliary or previous.endswith((
        "he's", "she's", "it's", "that's", "there's", "who's", "what's",
        "he’s", "she’s", "it’s", "that’s", "there’s", "who’s", "what’s",
    ))
    participle = word.endswith("ed") or word.endswith("en")
    participle = participle or word in IRREGULAR_PARTICIPLES
    if auxiliary and participle:
        return None, 0.65
    return None, 0.0

"""A partial, mixed lexical/phrase explanation of the first-layer component.

Processing compounds get positive scores; quantified data items and entity
names get negative scores. Small lexical, grammatical and formatting rules
capture additional regularities. These are additive training-fitted adjustments,
not a complete description of the component. State is just the previous token,
reset at document boundaries. Word rules lowercase text and remove leading
underscores, hyphens, periods and slashes; marker rules use the raw token.
"""
READS = ()


def words(s):
    return frozenset(s.split())


PROCESS = words('''process processing processor processors function functions fn
method methods operation operations algorithm algorithms analysis analytics
mining management protection transmission transfer transport transformation
conversion handling encoding decoding encoder decoder encryption collection
acquisition reduction flow service services model models command commands
syntax buffer buffers program programs query queries loop loops step steps
search count counting driven output input parameter parameters source sources
storage store controller control manipulation validation visualization security
backup sharing loader loading generator generation collector type types
structure structures filter filtering
处理 输出 函数 方法 分析 管理 传输 保护 服务 安全 转换 备份 增强 交换 采集
サービス 処理 関数 モデル 出力''')
ITEM = words('''character characters char chars letter letters word words
string strings element elements item items entry entries row rows column
columns field fields point points node nodes vertex vertices occurrence
occurrences observation observations value values key keys id ids identifier
identifiers name names filename filenames label labels frequency frequencies
coordinate coordinates phrase phrases 字符 字母 元素 条目 名称 名字 频率''')
ATOM = words('''character characters char chars letter letters word words
element elements occurrence occurrences observation observations phrase phrases
frequency frequencies''')
CHARACTER = words('character characters char chars letter letters 字符 字母')
OCCURRENCE = words('occurrence occurrences observation observations')
DATA = words('data input output copy search 数据 输入 输出 データ')
ENTITY = words('''file files column columns field fields variable variables
feature features string strings''')
QUANTIFIER = words('''each every all first last same duplicate duplicates unique
individual single one''')
NAME = words('name names named id ids identifier identifiers filename filenames')
DATA_FUNCTION = words('''function functions fn method methods model models
processing processor output 处理 输出 函数 方法 モデル 関数 処理''')
CONCRETE = ITEM | DATA | ENTITY
CONTAIN = words('contain contains containing have has that whose representing')
INPUT = words('input 输入 入力')
CALLABLE = words('function functions fn method methods 函数 方法 関数')

# Word families: preservation, calculation, information, examples, and amounts.
LEXICAL = (
    (words('keep keeping prevent preventing'), 0.099166),
    (words('''add added adding apply applied compute computing computation
calculate calculated calculating'''), -0.057100),
    (words('information knowledge'), 0.060178),
    (words('free freedom fun'), -0.078667),
    (words('case cases instance instances example examples'), 0.034794),
    (words('total sum quantity amount value number'), 0.038482),
    (words('back forward backward'), -0.065248),
    (words('large small high'), -0.048275),
)

# Adjustments on common grammatical continuations, given their preceding word.
GRAMMAR = {
    'example': ((words('for'), 0.092474),),
    'be': ((words('must'), -0.095204),
           (words('would may should might shall'), 0.044429),
           (words('can cannot to'), -0.016349)),
    'the': ((words('from by within between outside after around'), 0.035100),
            (words('when where how what which if using use'), -0.036376),
            (words('and that in'), -0.012643)),
    'to': ((words('likely possible supposed expected intended meant required'), 0.076957),
           (words('able unable need trying decided decides'), -0.038182)),
    'of': ((words('case form type series group process way'), 0.049576),
           (words('size length age time sum product derivative'), -0.054262),
           (ITEM, -0.026258)),
    'as': ((words('well same long large much'), -0.054132),),
}
MARKERS = {
    '<think>': 0.117421, '</think>': -0.000097,
    '<tool_call>': -0.084382, '</tool_call>': -0.063561,
    '</tool_response>': 0.103412,
    '<|im_start|>': -0.022466, '<|im_end|>': -0.024430,
    '<|endoftext|>': 0.012774, '，': 0.020524, '··': -0.082032,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, raw = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    w = raw.strip().lower().lstrip('_-./')
    p = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    value = 0.000417 + MARKERS.get(raw, 0.0)
    for family, amount in LEXICAL:
        if w in family:
            value += amount
    for antecedents, amount in GRAMMAR.get(w, ()):
        if p in antecedents:
            value += amount
    if w in PROCESS:
        value -= 0.000532
        if p in DATA:
            value += 0.169005
            if w in DATA_FUNCTION:
                value += 0.119634
                if p in INPUT and w in CALLABLE:
                    value += 0.018576
        if p in QUANTIFIER:
            value += 0.044955
            if p in {'each', 'every'}:
                value += 0.052922
    if w in ITEM:
        value -= 0.003860
        if p in QUANTIFIER:
            value -= 0.057322
            if w in ATOM:
                value -= 0.081457
                if w in CHARACTER:
                    value -= 0.085693
                if w in OCCURRENCE:
                    value -= 0.198287
        if p in ENTITY:
            value -= 0.047386
    if w in NAME and p in ENTITY:
        value -= 0.114626
        if p in {'column', 'columns'}:
            value -= 0.116659
    if p in CONCRETE:
        if w in {'in', 'with', 'as', 'that', 'whose', 'without'}:
            value -= 0.055830
        if w in CONTAIN:
            value -= 0.034962
    if '\\' in raw and raw.strip(' \\"') == '':
        value += -0.046457 if '"' in raw else 0.002926
    return (doc, w), float(value)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:2497 -- a diffuse, mostly-silent component.

What it does, in plain terms: this rank-one piece of layer 0's MLP output is almost
never important (causal importance > 0.1 at 6 of 10M tokens). Its activation is
small and of mixed sign on almost every token, and its sign does not follow any
simple word class, script, or punctuation pattern that we could find. The only
regularity with a clear sign is at the very first token of each document, where it
is mildly positive on average.

So this program predicts that small document-start value and 0 everywhere else.
It does not capture the per-token variation, which is token-identity specific and
has no short human-readable description.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START_MEAN = 0.0128  # mean activation at position 0 of a document, from training rows


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The position within the current document: 0 at a document's first token.
    t = prefix.position
    same_doc_as_prev = t > 0 and prefix.document_ids[t] == prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    value = 0.0 if same_doc_as_prev else DOC_START_MEAN
    return carry, float(value)

"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:2498 (Qwen3-1.7B, layer 0 MLP down projection).

What it does, in plain terms: it is a "coming into being / turning into" detector.
It goes clearly negative on the current token when that token is a word for forming,
creating, becoming or composing something, or the word "into" (as in "turn X into Y").
Examples: " form", " formed", " forming", " formation", " create", " created",
" creation", " became", " becoming", " composition", " into". Chinese 成 (become,
accomplish; as in 成为, 形成, 完成) and Korean 성 (as in 형성, 구성) push it most
negative. Almost every other token gives roughly zero.

The program looks only at the current token (no context, no state). It predicts:
  -1.0 for a "make/become" word, -0.6 for "into", -2.5 for a token containing 成 or 성,
   0 otherwise.
Predictions are negative because the component's activation is negative on these tokens.
"""

READS = ()

# English words for forming, creating, becoming or composing (whole words, lowercase).
MAKE_WORDS = {
    "form", "forms", "formed", "forming", "formation",
    "create", "creates", "created", "creating", "creation",
    "become", "becomes", "became", "becoming",
    "compose", "composed", "composition", "compositions",
    "constitute", "constitutes", "synthesis",
    "generate", "generated", "generating",
    "adult", "adults", "mature",
}

# Characters meaning "become / form / complete" in Chinese, and the Korean syllable 성 (as in 형성, 구성).
CJK_BECOME = set("成성")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word == "into":
        value = -0.6
    elif word in MAKE_WORDS:
        value = -1.0
    elif any(ch in CJK_BECOME for ch in token):
        value = -2.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

programs.haiku:
"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:2499, as a readable rule.

What it responds to, in plain terms:

1. Split characters (the main effect). The tokenizer is byte-level, so a
   character such as a Chinese or Japanese ideograph can be cut across two
   tokens. When a token ends partway through a character (the text so far now
   ends in an unfinished character, which decodes to U+FFFD), the component
   fires. It fires about 2.3 when the token starts with a space (" �"). Without
   a space it fires more strongly the more CJK text precedes it (about 2.8 in
   Latin-script context, up to about 6.4 after plenty of CJK). If the previous
   token was also left unfinished (a character spread over three or more
   tokens), it fires weakly, 2.0.
2. A few other tokens, weaker: the end-of-turn token <|im_end|> (2.3), the
   stems of English negative contractions ("don" in "don't", "didn", "isn",
   ... about 1.1), tokens ending in a backslash (escape sequences in code,
   about 0.6), and code/HTML symbols and carriage returns (about 1.0).

Everything else predicts 0. The numbers are rough averages measured on
training text; the rule is a summary, not a fit to the component's exact values.
"""

READS = ()

IM_END = "<|im_end|>"
NEGATIVE_STEMS = {" don", " doesn", " didn", " isn", " couldn", " wasn", " wouldn",
                  " aren", " hadn", " hasn", " shouldn"}
CODE_SYMBOLS = {"\r", " &", "&", " &&", "&&", "&#", "</"}


def is_cjk(ch):
    """Han ideographs, Japanese kana and Hangul syllables."""
    return ("぀" <= ch <= "ヿ" or "一" <= ch <= "鿿"
            or "가" <= ch <= "힯")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]          # the row's text up to this token
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]         # this token alone
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    before = "" if new_doc else prefix.text_prefixes[-2]

    if text.endswith("�"):              # this token leaves a character unfinished
        if before.endswith("�"):        # ...and the previous one was unfinished too
            return None, 2.0
        if token.startswith(" "):
            return None, 2.3
        recent = before.replace("�", "")[-12:]
        cjk = sum(is_cjk(c) for c in recent) / max(1, len(recent))
        return None, 2.8 + 3.6 * cjk
    if token == IM_END:
        return None, 2.3
    if token in NEGATIVE_STEMS:
        return None, 1.1
    if token.endswith("\\"):
        return None, 0.6
    if token in CODE_SYMBOLS:
        return None, 1.0
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 2500: a weak, mostly token-specific signal.

What it does: this component is almost silent. Its activation has std 0.03 and is
dominated by no single kind of token. The only broad patterns found in the data are
small per-class offsets, so this program predicts a small constant per broad token class
(CJK characters, spaces, '.'-prefixed identifiers, digits, newlines, plain words, and
other symbols), plus a small negative offset on the first token of each document.

Why these classes: they are the readable groups with any sign in the data. The offsets
are means measured on training text. Their held-out variance explained is about 0.001,
so this program is essentially a zero prediction with a light class-based tilt.
The per-token table this component is really tied to (token identity, about 0.3 held-out
variance explained, but spread over tens of thousands of tokens with no shared concept)
is not included here.
"""

READS = ()

# mean activation per broad token class, measured on training text
CLASS_MEAN = {
    "space": 0.0023,
    "newline": -0.0016,
    "cjk": 0.0031,
    "digit": 0.0011,
    "dot": 0.0033,
    "word": -0.0006,
    "other": 0.0,
}
DOC_START = -0.008  # first token of a document


def token_class(s):
    if s.strip() == "":
        return "space"
    if "\n" in s:
        return "newline"
    if any("぀" <= c <= "ヿ" or "㐀" <= c <= "鿿" or "가" <= c <= "힯" for c in s):
        return "cjk"
    if s.strip().isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if s.lstrip().startswith("."):
        return "dot"
    if s.isascii() and s.strip().isalpha():
        return "word"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        return None, DOC_START
    return None, CLASS_MEAN[token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

programs.haiku:
"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:2503 — a "re-/rem-/ren- word fragment" detector.

What the component does, in plain terms
---------------------------------------
Its activation is almost entirely a function of the current token. It is strongly
NEGATIVE on short word-start fragments spelled r-e-m or r-e-n (" rem", "rem", "Rem",
"REM", "ren", " Ren", "/rem"): tokens the tokenizer cut out of the middle of a longer word,
such as " rem" in "rem|odelling", "rem|édio", "ren|ounced" or "rem|ixContext". Weaker
negatives come on other r-e-words (" re", " ret", " rec", " rev", "review", "rename",
"remove", "remain", ...). It is POSITIVE on " piece" and " pieces" (about +1).
Almost everywhere else it is near zero.

The program is a lookup on the newest token's spelling, with a few spelling families.
It reads only the newest token (no state, no context).

Main program: `step` below. The values are the mean activations measured on training rows.
"""

READS = ()

# Exact fragments, lower-cased with the leading space stripped.
FRAGMENT_VALUE = {"rem": -4.5, "ren": -2.5, "piece": 1.1, "pieces": 1.1}
# Short r-e pieces and whole r-e words that are weakly negative.
SHORT_RE_VALUE = {"re": -0.5, "ret": -0.5, "rec": -0.5, "rel": -0.5, "rent": -0.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in FRAGMENT_VALUE:
        value = FRAGMENT_VALUE[word]
    elif word in SHORT_RE_VALUE:
        value = SHORT_RE_VALUE[word]
    elif word.startswith("rem"):          # remove, remain, reminder, remark ...
        value = -0.7
    elif word.startswith("ren"):          # rename, renal, renew ...
        value = -0.5
    elif word.startswith("rev") or word.startswith("review"):
        value = -0.5
    else:

captures the "inside Swedish text" boost. The memory resets at each document boundary.

closing quote) gets only a weak -0.7. It is near zero on quote marks used as code or JSON delimiters (after a colon, comma, =, {, etc.),

how many are ordinary words (letters only). Two or fewer words means no firing; five or
more means full strength; in between it scales up linearly.

    ' "': -4.0,   # straight double quote after a space
    ' “': -3.9,   # curly double quote after a space
    ' ‘': -3.0,   # curly single quote after a space
    ' \'': -2.7,  # straight single quote after a space
    ' „': -2.7,   # German low-9 quote
    ' «': -2.3,   # guillemet
    ' ("': -2.2,  # quote opened inside parentheses
    ' (“': -2.7,
    '「': -1.8,   # Japanese corner bracket
    '“': -1.4,    # curly quote with no space before it
    '"': -0.7,    # straight quote with no space before it (mostly closing quotes)

FULL_WORDS = 5      # this many plain-word tokens in the window give full strength
NO_WORDS = 2        # this many or fewer give no firing

"""Approximate the negative response to quantitative questions and calculations.

What/how and requests to find a result respond more strongly after numerical
facts, measurements, or mathematical vocabulary. Headings and explanatory
verbs weaken the response. Amount words retain some of the preceding response;
'why' has a small positive baseline. Most small lexical variation is omitted.
"""
import re

READS = ()
REQUESTS = {'find', 'calculate', 'determine'}
MATH = set('''number numbers equation equations probability ratio fraction percent
percentage speed velocity acceleration height length width area volume mass force
distance angle radius spring interest profit cost rate sum total average mean
perimeter rectangle triangle square cube slope function coefficient factor factors
polynomial votes tickets kg cm km mph meters metres pounds dollars minutes
seconds hours'''.split())
NUMERALS = set('''one two three four five six seven eight nine ten hundred
thousand twice'''.split())
EXPLANATION = set('''show shows showing shown explain explains explained demonstrate
demonstrates learn learning know knows understand understanding describe describes
notice see check remember illustrate illustrates tell'''.split())
WORDS = re.compile(r'\b\w+\b')
LAST_WORD = re.compile(r'([^\W\d_]+)$')
NUMBERS = re.compile(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d+)*')
UNITS = re.compile(r'\d\s*(?:m|s|N|K|V|g|kg|cm|km|ft|in|lb|°C|°|%)(?!\w)')


def context_response(text):
    words = WORDS.findall(text.lower())
    value = -0.06 * min(4, len(NUMBERS.findall(text)))
    value -= 0.08 * min(4, sum(w in MATH for w in words))
    value -= 0.06 * min(3, sum(w in NUMERALS for w in words))
    value -= 0.22 * bool(UNITS.search(text))
    value -= 0.21 * bool(re.search(r'[.!?,;]\s*$', text))
    value += 0.14 * bool(re.match(r'^\s*#+\s*$', text.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]))
    value += 0.09 * ('\n' in text[-8:])
    value += 0.14 * bool(words and words[-1] in EXPLANATION)
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        context, previous_word, previous_value = '', '', 0.0
    else:
        _, context, previous_word, previous_value = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = (context + token)[-140:]
    word = token.strip()
    joined = not token[:1].isspace()
    match = LAST_WORD.search(text)
    if word and match and len(match[1]) > len(word) and not token[:1].isspace():
        word = match[1]  # Complete words split across tokens, e.g. C + alculate.
        context = context[:-(len(word) - len(token))]
        joined = not context[-1:].isspace()
    lower = word.lower()
    capital = word[:1].isupper()
    value = 0.0
    if lower in {'what', 'how', 'как'} | REQUESTS | {'if', 'assume', 'assuming'}:
        response = context_response(context)
        if lower in {'what', 'how', 'как'}:
            value = -0.05 if lower == 'what' else 0.03
            value -= (0.10 if lower == 'what' else 0.16) * capital
            value += 0.08 * joined + response
        elif lower in REQUESTS:
            value = -0.06 - 0.17 * capital + 0.07 * joined + 0.6 * response
        else:
            value = 0.03 - (0.20 if lower != 'if' else 0.0) * capital
            value += (0.35 if capital else 0.15) * response
    elif lower in {'many', 'much', 'percent', 'rate'}:
        value = {'many': -0.025, 'much': 0.01,

        if previous_word in {'what', 'how'}:
            value = (-0.21 if lower == 'many' else -0.09)
            value += 0.35 * min(0.0, previous_value)
    elif lower == 'why':
        value = -0.01 if capital else 0.12
    elif lower == 'compounded':
        value = -0.35
    return (doc, text, lower, value), float(value)

starts a sentence: "What" in "What is the probability ...", "How" in "How many votes ...",

    "<|im_end|>": -5.5,

    "</think>": -5.8,
    "<tool_call>": -6.9,
    "</tool_call>": -3.9,
    "<tool_response>": -5.7,
    "</tool_response>": -5.3,

# optionally preceded by a space or a dot.

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    return carry, 0.0

What it does: this component responds weakly to the vocabulary of formal Chinese
policy and official speech (发展, 建设, 不断, 人民群众, 现代化, 伟大, ...), and most
strongly to the conjunction 和 when it joins such abstract nouns in formal text
("...共同富裕和现代化..."). It is near zero on everyday text and on programming text.

The program predicts, per token:
- 0.125 for a token containing a policy-register word (CORE below);
- for 和 ("and"): 0.04 plus 0.04 for each policy-register token among the 24
  tokens before it, so 和 is strongest when the passage is already formal;
- 0 otherwise.

The word list is a concept (policy and official vocabulary), written by hand from
the tokens that activate the component most. The context window is reset at each
document boundary, as the model does. Amplitudes are half of the least-squares
fit, which keeps the edit's effect on the model's output at or below switching
the component off.
"""

WINDOW = 24
CONJ = "和"
CORE = (
    "发展 建设 创新 推进 推动 不断 提高 提升 能力 水平 融合 思想 理念 斗争 伟大 "
    "坚定 坚持 富裕 宗旨 执政 新时代 高质量 现代化 战略 变革 制度 实现 人民群众 "
    "奋斗 奋进 大局 贯穿 促进 增长 体系 事业 成果 增强 理想信念 改革 机制 生态 "
    "和谐 形势 矛盾 利益 全局 生产力 民族 复兴 与时俱进 以人为本 深入人心 "
    "实事求是 工作 质量 服务 管理 完善 加强 保障 落实 部署 政策 产业 市场 环境 "
    "企业 城市 教育 人才 责任 目标 任务 要求 作用"
).split()


def is_core(token):
    return len(token) >= 2 and any(word in token for word in CORE)

        value = 0.0
    return carry, value
